candidates.attacker_control: The {name}, {profile} and {label} path variables of GET /{name}/{profile}/{label}, /{label}/{name}-{profiles}.{properties|json|yml|yaml} and GET /{name}/{profile}/{label}/** are fully attacker-controlled. EnvironmentController only runs PathUtils.isInvalidEncodedLocation+Environment.normalize on name and label (profiles is never validated), and ResourceController only applies Environment.normalize (which merely maps '(_)' to '/'), so values containing '/', ':', '@', '.', '%' etc. reach the git repository layer.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The placeholder feature itself is intentional and documented, so a substituted value is expected. For the most common template form (placeholder in the path, e.g. https://github.com/org/{application}.git) URL parsing keeps the original host, so '..', '@' or ':' inside the value cannot by itself move the authority, which limits the issue to templates with an authority/user-info-position placeholder - a deployment-specific configuration I could not verify here. I also verified that the request values cannot pre-validate themselves away: no PathUtils/host check exists on the expanded URI (AbstractScmAccessor.setUri only normalizes slashes), and profiles is not validated at all in EnvironmentController. I did not execute any code, so URL/JGit parsing behaviour for crafted values is unverified.
candidates.impact: Server-side outbound request to an attacker-influenced location (SSRF: port/host scanning, requests to internal services via the config server's network position) and, when the placeholder occupies the user-info/authority position, transmission of the repository's configured git username/password to a host chosen by the attacker. Secondary: unbounded growth of the placeholders map enables memory-exhaustion denial of service from repeated distinct values.
candidates.prerequisites: Git backend configured with a URI (or repos.<name>.uri) containing a placeholder that can affect the URI authority (subdomain or user-info position); the server is reachable so that a request for an arbitrary application/profile/label reaches the git-based EnvironmentRepository (standard /{name}/{profile}/{label} or /{name}/{profile}/{label}/** endpoints).
candidates.root_cause: MultipleJGitEnvironmentRepository.getRepository(JGitEnvironmentRepository, String application, String profile, String label) takes the request path variables and performs plain String.replace on the configured repository URI template ({application}, {profile}, {label}); the only guard is that the template contains '{'. setUri() then merely strips trailing slashes / appends a context path and does no authority validation, and the expanded URI is used to clone/fetch. A placeholder that sits before the path separator (authority or user-info position, e.g. https://{application}@host/org/repo.git or https://{application}.example.com/repo.git) lets the substituted value redirect the request to an attacker-chosen host/userinfo while the repository's configured username/password are still attached by GitCredentialsProviderFactory.createFor(expandedUri, ...).
candidates.title: Attacker-controlled application/profile/label interpolated into configured git repository URI templates (URI/host injection, SSRF + credential exposure)
candidates.trace: HTTP request path variables -> EnvironmentController.labelled (normalize name/label only) / ResourceController.retrieve (Environment.normalize only) -> repository.findOne/getLocations -> MultipleJGitEnvironmentRepository.findOne/getLocations -> getRepositories -> getRepository(repository, application, profile, label): key = template URI with {application}/{profile}/{label} replaced by attacker values (lines 212-223) -> getRepository(source, key) -> BeanUtils.copyProperties + setUri(key) -> JGitEnvironmentRepository.refresh/cloneToBasedir/fetch use the expanded URI as remote; configureCommand -> GitCredentialsProviderFactory.createFor(expandedUri, username, password, ...) attaches the configured credentials to the outbound request. The expanded key is also cached in the unbounded 'placeholders' map (line 224-227).
candidates.unverified: Whether any deployment uses an authority-affecting placeholder template; exact behaviour of java.net/JGit URI parsing for crafted values (user-info injection, '#'/'?' truncation, IDN/':' handling); whether the dataset's ground-truth configuration exercises this code path; no runtime confirmation of SSRF or credential disclosure.
candidates.weakness_type: Server-Side Request Forgery / URI injection via unvalidated template substitution (CWE-918, CWE-74)

coverage_summary: Scope: 162 repository files (139 Java) across spring-cloud-config-server, -client, -monitor, -sample, -dependencies/starters, build files, and two docs files; tests and most asciidoc docs are not part of the snapshot. I read the security-relevant Java in full or near-full: PathUtils, ResourceController/GenericResourceRepository/ResourceRepositoryConfiguration, EnvironmentController, NativeEnvironmentRepository, JGitEnvironmentRepository, MultipleJGitEnvironmentRepository(+Factory/Properties), AbstractScmAccessor(+Properties), SvnKitEnvironmentRepository, JdbcEnvironmentRepository, VaultEnvironmentRepository(+Properties/Factory/KvAccessStrategy*), CredhubEnvironmentRepository, Composite*/SearchPath*, EnvironmentEncryptorEnvironmentRepository, CipherEnvironmentEncryptor, EncryptionController, EncryptionAutoConfiguration, KeyStore/SingleTextEncryptorLocator, all monitor extractors + PropertyPathEndpoint + FileMonitorConfiguration, ConfigServicePropertySourceLocator, ConfigClientProperties, client bootstrap/health/watch classes, AWS CodeCommit provider, git credential providers, HTTP/proxy helpers, and the ssh validators/session factories. P1 index reports partial coverage: 159/162 files indexed, 3 source files missing from the index, no control-flow/data-flow or semantic resolution (1842 unresolved calls), Spring annotations are name-based only, and the index is explicitly not SAST; no index label was treated as a verdict.
limitations: No code, tests, or scanners were executed; all reachability/impact statements are static-source inferences.

No diff against upstream was possible, so I could not confirm which hunks (if any) were removed/injected; version conclusions rest on pom versions (2.1.8.RELEASE, spring-cloud-build 2.1.11.RELEASE) and on code patterns.
Tests are absent from the snapshot, so the expected/forbidden inputs for the path-validation code could not be cross-checked.

The submitted candidate is configuration-dependent: I could not verify any deployment's git URI template form, so SSRF/credential-exposure impact is a plausible lead, not a demonstrated vulnerability.

Some files were only skimmed (several ssh validators, property/DTO classes, monitor extractors, sample application, docs/build files) and the P1 index omitted 3 files; these areas should not be considered fully audited.
The candidate maps to one root cause only; the rejected leads are listed for completeness and are not independent findings.

rejected_leads.lead: Directory traversal / arbitrary file read through the resource endpoint (ResourceController.getFilePath stem logic, GenericResourceRepository.getProfilePaths, NativeEnvironmentRepository addLabelLocations, SvnKitEnvironmentRepository.getSvnPath(workingDirectory, label) with label = '..(_)..(_)...').
rejected_leads.reason: The traversal defences are present in this snapshot and I verified them in source: PathUtils.isInvalidEncodedLocation/isInvalidEncodedPath decode the value again and reject '..', '#'; GenericResourceRepository.findOne skips any location containing '..' before resolving the relative path; EnvironmentController.normalize rejects '..'/'#' for name and label. The remaining gap is a defense-in-depth ordering issue in SvnKitEnvironmentRepository.getSvnPath (label resolved to a File before the location check) and the unvalidated 'profiles' variable - without a demonstrated read of a file outside the search location, these do not meet the evidence bar.

rejected_leads.lead: Unvalidated 'profiles' path variable (EnvironmentController.labelled passes profiles to repositories without normalize/PathUtils check; it is substituted into {profile} search-location/URI placeholders, Vault key paths and CredHub '/{app}/{profile}/{label}' paths).
rejected_leads.reason: Same root idea as the submitted candidate and gated on non-default configuration ({profile} placeholder in search paths/URI templates, or a backend whose API resolves '..'); not separately demonstrable from source as a distinct exploitable issue.

The SQL text comes from configuration (spring.cloud.config.server.jdbc.sql) and is executed with bound parameters (jdbc.query(sql, new Object[]{app, env, label}, extractor)); request values are not concatenated into SQL.

rejected_leads.lead: TLS/host verification bypass helpers (HttpClientSupport.java:50-53 trust-all SSLContext + NoopHostnameVerifier; GitSkipSslValidationCredentialsProvider answering JGit trust prompts).
rejected_leads.reason: Both are gated behind the explicit spring.cloud.config.server.git.skip-ssl-validation / vault.skip-ssl-validation opt-in properties (default false) and are documented test/dev conveniences.

rejected_leads.lead: KeyStoreTextEncryptorLocator.locate() selecting a keystore alias from request-supplied {key:...} prefixes (/decrypt|/encrypt endpoints).
rejected_leads.reason: Matches the upstream design (per-application/profile key lookup); it requires the /encrypt|/decrypt endpoints to be reachable and a keystore to be configured, and I found no source evidence that it bypasses a configured key policy in this snapshot.
Present in the client DTO and matches the upstream implementation; it is a logging-hygiene concern rather than an attacker-reachable vulnerability.

summary: Reviewed the spring-cloud-config snapshot (poms indicate the 2.1.8.RELEASE line; 162 files, 139 Java, server + client + monitor modules). I traced request-controlled path variables (/{name}/{profile}/{label}) through the controllers, environment repositories, resource repository, and git/vault/credhub backends. The project's principal known-weak area (path traversal in the resource/environment serving code) is mitigated in this snapshot: PathUtils carries decoded/processed traversal checks and both call sites are present (GenericResourceRepository skips locations containing ".."; EnvironmentController.normalize rejects ".."/"#"). The strongest remaining, source-supported issue is that attacker-controlled application/profile/label values are interpolated into configured git URI templates and the resulting URI is used for outbound git operations with configured credentials, with no validation that the expansion cannot move the URI authority.
